content.user_title: Write Reliable AI Skills With TDD
content.value_statement: AI skill instructions can be vague, untested, and hard to reuse. This skill guides test-first skill writing with subagent pressure tests.
actual_capabilities: Maps test-driven development to skill creation with RED, GREEN, and REFACTOR phases.
Shows how to write focused SKILL.md frontmatter, descriptions, examples, and checklists.
Explains how to test skills with baseline and post-skill subagent scenarios.
Provides search optimization guidance for Claude skill discovery.
Guides reference file organization, flowchart usage, and deployment checks.
Includes persuasion principles for discipline-enforcing documentation.
limitations: It is guidance documentation, not an automated skill generator.
It assumes access to subagents or comparable test sessions.
It focuses on Claude-style skill files and may need adaptation for other systems.
It does not guarantee marketplace acceptance or publish skills automatically.

use_cases.title: Create a New Skill
use_cases.description: Plan triggers, baseline failures, and a minimal skill document before writing final instructions.

use_cases.title: Repair a Weak Skill
use_cases.description: Find vague guidance, missing examples, and rationalization gaps in an existing skill.

use_cases.title: Validate Before Release
use_cases.description: Use pressure scenarios, quality checks, and deployment steps before sharing a skill.

prompt_templates.title: Create a First Draft
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the writing-skills process to plan a new skill for [topic]. Start with triggering conditions, expected behavior, and a minimal SKILL.md outline.

prompt_templates.title: Run Baseline Tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Design three pressure scenarios for a skill that teaches [discipline]. Show what to test before writing or editing the skill.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Discoverability
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this skill description and section structure for Claude search optimization. Suggest concise edits that improve triggering and reduce context use.

prompt_templates.title: Audit and Refactor
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply the RED-GREEN-REFACTOR process to this existing skill. Identify missing tests, likely rationalizations, reference file issues, and deployment blockers.

output_examples.input: I need a skill for avoiding arbitrary waits in tests.
output: Proposed trigger: use when tests have race conditions or timing-dependent failures.
Baseline test: ask an agent to fix a flaky async test under time pressure.
Minimal outline: overview, rule, good example, rationalization table, and release checklist.

output_examples.input: My skill has long examples and a weak description.
output: Rewrite the description around concrete symptoms and user triggers.
Move heavy details into one-level reference files.
Keep one strong example that agents can adapt safely.

output_examples.input: Check a discipline skill before release.
output: Run baseline scenarios without the skill and record the failure patterns.
Run the same scenarios with the skill and compare compliance.
Add explicit counters for any new rationalizations.

best_practices: Run baseline tests before editing skill text.
Keep examples focused, complete, and directly tied to the skill behavior.
Use one-level reference files for heavy material.
anti_patterns: Writing a skill because the topic feels useful, without a failing scenario.
Putting long references, many examples, and deployment steps into one dense file.
Using authority language without testing whether agents follow it.

faq.question: Does this skill write the skill for me?
faq.answer: It guides the process. You still choose the behavior, examples, tests, and final wording.

faq.question: Why test skill instructions with subagents?
faq.answer: Subagents reveal how instructions fail under pressure before the skill reaches daily use.

faq.question: Can I use it with Codex or Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The concepts apply to Codex, Claude, and Claude Code, but file conventions may differ.

faq.question: Does it require executable scripts?
faq.answer: No. It supports documentation-only skills and explains when separate scripts or references are useful.

faq.question: Is it only for new skills?
faq.answer: No. It also covers edits, refactors, discovery improvements, and pre-release checks.

faq.question: How should I handle a large reference?
faq.answer: Keep the overview in SKILL.md and link one level deep to focused reference files.
